findings.element: 2026 consensus brackets table — 'KEY VIEW' column
findings.detail: The 'Key View' column text is visibly cut off for every institution row (e.g., Goldman Sachs shows 'fading tariff drag growth, below-c', BCA Research shows 'Two-stage 2026: tech, broad selloff HQ as labo oil, tech capex t', Blue Chip Consensus shows 'Central tendency: T'). The column container is too narrow to display the full commentary, making a key qualitative field unreadable in a board-level deck.

findings.element: Sector panels (all 12 sector tiles) — commentary bullet text
findings.detail: The bullet-point commentary beneath each sector tile (e.g., Passenger Airlines, Hotels & Accommodations, Restaurants & Food Svcs, etc.) is rendered at an extremely small font size — estimated 6–7 px — making it completely illegible at normal viewing distance. This content would be unreadable in a board presentation.

findings.element: Six 2026 themes anchor section — body paragraphs
findings.detail: The numbered theme paragraphs (①–⑥) at the bottom of the tab are rendered at a very small font size, making the detailed commentary difficult to read without zooming in. At board-deck resolution this would be flagged immediately.

findings.element: Source attribution lines (all charts and tables)
findings.detail: Source lines beneath charts and the consensus table are rendered at approximately 5–6 px, well below any legible threshold. While source lines are typically small, they are completely unreadable here.

findings.element: Sector tiles — SNP 2026 / GDP 2026F metric labels
findings.detail: Several sector tile header labels (e.g., 'SNP 2026', 'GDP 2026F') appear compressed and partially cut off within their tile containers, particularly in the second row of sector panels (Software & Cloud, Pharmaceuticals/GLP-1, Residential Real Estate, Commercial RE, Auto Manufacturing).

findings.element: Exhibit 01 — Quarterly GDP chart 'So what' note
findings.detail: The 'So what' commentary block appears below the chart rather than above it, preceding the first chart as required. The note follows the bar chart instead of introducing it.

findings.element: Exhibit 02 — Consensus indicators chart 'So what' note
findings.detail: The 'So what' commentary block is placed below the grouped bar chart rather than above it, violating the rule that per-tab fc-note commentary must precede the first chart.

findings.element: Sector panels grid — row spacing
findings.detail: The vertical spacing between the three rows of sector panels is visibly uneven — the gap between row 1 (Airlines through E-Commerce) and row 2 (Software through Auto Manufacturing) appears tighter than the gap between row 2 and row 3 (Federal Government, Freight & Logistics), creating inconsistent panel rhythm.

findings.element: Sector panel mini-charts — bar labels and commentary text
findings.detail: The per-sector panel commentary lines (e.g., 'State/Local partially offsetting federal contraction…') and the small bar-chart axis labels (2022–2025 year ticks) are rendered at approximately 7–8 px, well below the minimum legible size for a board-deck display. A senior reviewer reading a printed or projected version would be unable to read these without zooming.

findings.element: Bottom footnote / source line
findings.detail: The full-width footnote row at the very bottom of the tab ('Sources: BEA GDP PCE; BLS CPI Jobs; Wages; Unemployment…') is rendered in extremely small, low-contrast grey text (~6–7 px). It is effectively unreadable at normal viewing distance and would not survive projection or printing.

findings.element: Federal Govt sector panel — commentary text
findings.detail: The commentary line beneath the Federal Govt mini-chart appears to be cut off mid-sentence ('…2026 2020 annual CBO est. 2025 Damp data due — fed workers transfer while, or are contractors not counted in payrolls.'). The text overflows or is clipped at the panel boundary, making the sentence incomplete.

findings.element: GDP Commentary — 2025 Growth & 2026 Outlook (fc-note box)
findings.detail: The commentary block contains hedging filler language ('cannot be ruled out if current conditions persist') and runs to approximately 5–6 readable sentences, exceeding the 2–4 sentence limit. Style guide §2 caps per-tab commentary at four sentences.

findings.element: Sector panel grid — bottom row (Cruise Lines / Travel Agencies)
findings.detail: The bottom row contains only two panels (Cruise Lines and Travel Agencies) while all other rows contain six panels, leaving a large blank area to the right. This asymmetric trailing row creates a visually unbalanced layout that would be noticeable in a board presentation.

findings.element: Annual GDP contribution table vs. sector panel grid
findings.detail: The vertical gap between the last row of sector mini-chart panels and the 'Real GDP held 2.0% in 2025' summary table is noticeably larger than the inter-panel gaps within the grid, creating an inconsistent rhythm between dashboard sections.

findings.element: Sector mini-chart bar charts (all panels)
findings.detail: Each sector panel contains a small grouped bar chart with two or three color-coded bar series (teal, red/pink, orange, blue). No legend is present within or adjacent to any panel explaining what each color represents. A board audience cannot decode the color encoding without a legend.

findings.element: Sector panel trend sparklines — negative/positive color coding
findings.detail: Several panels use orange to indicate a negative or warning trend (e.g., Autos, Pharma/Biotech), while others use red for the same semantic role. The inconsistent use of orange vs. red for 'negative/critical' values conflicts with a single defined critical color and may confuse readers.

findings.element: Jobs tab
findings.detail: No visual defects detected

findings.element: Unemployment tab
findings.detail: No visual defects detected

findings.element: TOP SECTOR metric tile
findings.detail: The 'Top Sector' KPI card displays 'Investmen t Banking' with a line break mid-word, making it appear as two words across two lines. This is a clear text overflow/truncation rendering error visible at CEO level.

findings.element: EX 4 Sector wage growth horizontal bar chart — x-axis labels
findings.detail: The x-axis tick labels on the sector bar chart (right panel, EX 4) appear compressed and difficult to read at dashboard resolution, with values crowding near the axis baseline.

findings.element: Source footnotes across all chart panels
findings.detail: Source attribution text at the bottom of EX 2, EX 3, EX 4, and the sector table is rendered at an extremely small font size (appears sub-7pt), making it effectively unreadable in a board deck context.

findings.element: Bottom page-level source line
findings.detail: The full-width source citation line at the very bottom of the page is rendered at a font size so small it is completely illegible, even at full screenshot resolution.

findings.element: EX 2 'So what' callout text
findings.detail: The 'So what' insight line reads: 'A thinning real-wage cushion plus 3.6% savings rate means consumer spending is increasingly drawn from buffers — vulnerable to any renewed inflation impulse.' This is a single sentence, falling below the style guide minimum of 2 sentences for fc-note commentary.

findings.element: EX 3 and EX 4 side-by-side panels
findings.detail: The vertical height of the EX 3 chart panel (left) appears noticeably taller than the EX 4 bar chart panel (right), creating an uneven bottom alignment between the two peer panels on the same row.

findings.element: EX 3 Real wages line chart
findings.detail: The EX 3 chart shows only approximately 5 annual data points (2021–2025/2026) for both the nominal and real series. While annual cadence may be intentional, the dashed real series appears to have only 4 plotted points with large gaps, which may mislead viewers about data continuity.

findings.element: Exhibit 5 – 'Goods inflation has normalised' horizontal bar chart, category labels
findings.detail: Several category labels on the left axis (e.g., 'Transportation Svcs', 'Food Away From Home') appear clipped or abbreviated mid-word, making them hard to read at board-deck resolution.

findings.element: Exhibit 4 – Annual CPI bar chart, x-axis year labels
findings.detail: Year labels along the x-axis (1988–2025) are rendered at an extremely small font size and are difficult to read without zooming in, which is unacceptable for a CEO/board audience.

findings.element: Footer / data-source line at the very bottom of the tab
findings.detail: The consolidated source line spanning the full width of the page is rendered in a font size that is effectively illegible (~6–7 px equivalent), well below the style-guide minimum for body/caption text.

findings.element: Exhibit 7 – Trimmed-mean & median CPI line chart, data-point callout labels
findings.detail: Multiple inline value callouts (e.g., the cluster of labels near the 2022–2023 peak and again at the right-hand tail) overlap each other and the lines, making individual values unreadable.

findings.element: KPI tile – 'STICKIEST' category tile ('Transportation Svcs')
findings.detail: The category name 'Transportation Svcs' wraps awkwardly and the '+6.1%' sub-label is visually cramped; at smaller viewport sizes the text risks being clipped by the tile boundary.

findings.element: Exhibit 2 'So what' callout – '…The 90bp headline/core gap is entirely energy-driven…'
findings.detail: The 'So what' sentence is a single sentence, falling below the style-guide minimum of 2 sentences for per-chart commentary callouts.

findings.element: Exhibit 3 'So what' callout – '…Acceleration is concentrated in energy-adjacent categories…'
findings.detail: Again only one sentence is present in the 'So what' box, violating the 2-sentence minimum.

findings.element: Gap between Exhibit 6 (category table) and Exhibit 7 (trimmed-mean chart)
findings.detail: The vertical gap between the Exhibit 6 table panel and the Exhibit 7 chart panel is noticeably larger than the gap between other adjacent panels on the same tab, creating an uneven rhythm.

findings.element: EX 2 dual-panel chart — axis labels and data point annotations
findings.detail: The x-axis tick labels, y-axis labels, and inline data annotations on both the Case-Shiller YoY panel and the 30yr Mortgage Rate panel are extremely small and difficult to read at dashboard viewing scale. A board-level audience would struggle to extract values without zooming in.

findings.element: EX 3 Home prices vs. FHFA — axis labels and source note
findings.detail: Axis tick labels, the index value annotations (e.g. '77 / 79.7k'), and the source footnote text are rendered at a size that is illegible without zooming. Critical for a CEO-level deck.

findings.element: EX 4 Mortgage rate gap to Fed funds — axis labels and data point dots
findings.detail: Year labels on the x-axis and rate values on the y-axis are too small to read comfortably. The dense dot-connected series compounds the illegibility.

findings.element: EX 5 Housing starts bar chart — x-axis year labels
findings.detail: Annual year labels along the x-axis are rendered at a very small font size and appear crowded, making individual years hard to distinguish.

findings.element: EX 6 Affordability index dual-panel — axis labels and bar annotations
findings.detail: Both the affordability index panel and the months-supply panel have axis labels and inline annotations that are too small to read at normal viewing distance, undermining the chart's utility in a board presentation.

findings.element: EX 7 Metro table — source footnote block at bottom
findings.detail: The multi-line source citation at the very bottom of the metro table is rendered in an extremely small font, effectively unreadable without magnification.

findings.element: Global footer — data-source line at page bottom
findings.detail: The footer source line ('Sources: BEA GDP/PCE; BLS CPI…') is rendered at a size that is illegible at normal screen resolution, which is a concern if the deck is printed or projected.

findings.element: EX 5 Housing starts — x-axis year labels
findings.detail: With ~30 annual bars compressed into the panel width, x-axis year labels visibly crowd and partially overlap each other, making the time axis hard to parse.

findings.element: EX 4 Mortgage rate gap — x-axis decade labels
findings.detail: Year labels on the long historical x-axis (1990–2020+) appear to run together in the compressed panel, reducing readability.

findings.element: EX 2 dual-panel chart — vertical spacing between top and bottom sub-panels
findings.detail: The gap between the Case-Shiller YoY panel and the 30yr Mortgage Rate panel appears tighter than the standard inter-panel spacing used elsewhere on the tab, creating a visually cramped exhibit.

findings.element: EX 1 Housing Commentary — opening paragraph
findings.detail: The commentary block contains five sentences, exceeding the maximum of four permitted sentences per style_guide §2. ('The 30Y mortgage rate… Housing starts at 1.22M show the market has not yet fully capitulated, but the pipeline will thin materially as builder confidence erodes under these financing conditions. The Case-Shiller HPI uptick of 143bp is a lagging artifact of constrained supply, not a signal of demand strength — do not interpret it as housing resilience.' counts as five discrete sentences.)

findings.element: EX 6 Affordability index — top panel (affordability index bars)
findings.detail: The top affordability-index panel shows bars with at least two apparent color states (normal vs. highlighted recent bars) but no legend is visible within the panel to explain the color encoding, leaving the reader to guess the distinction.

findings.element: Oil Supply Shock Tracker — Daily Closes chart (Section 2, Exhibit 5)
findings.detail: X-axis date labels along the bottom of the daily closes chart are extremely small and densely packed across 170 sessions, making individual dates unreadable at dashboard viewing scale.

findings.element: Full Oil Impact Chain table (Section 2, Exhibit 6) — node detail rows
findings.detail: The descriptive sub-text beneath each phase node (e.g., 'Describes most moves within days of a shock…') is rendered at a very small font size, making it illegible without zooming in, inappropriate for a CEO/board-level deck.

findings.element: Source attribution lines throughout (Sections 1–4)
findings.detail: Source lines (e.g., 'SOURCE: ENERGY INFORMATION ADMINISTRATION (EIA)…') are rendered in very light gray at an extremely small point size, falling below the minimum contrast and size threshold for board-level materials.

findings.element: Footer data-source strip at the very bottom of the dashboard
findings.detail: The full-width footer listing all data sources (BEA, BLS, Fed, EIA, etc.) is rendered in a single dense line of very small text that is effectively unreadable, which would draw criticism in a board review.

findings.element: Section 4 — Exhibit 7 recession history chart, X-axis labels
findings.detail: Year labels on the X-axis of the annual WTI/recession history chart (1973–2025) appear tightly packed and likely overlap or are clipped at the left and right edges, reducing readability.

findings.element: Section 4 — Exhibit 8 historical shocks table, 'Economic Consequence' column
findings.detail: The 'Economic Consequence' column text (e.g., 'Stagflation GDP -2.7% Inflation 12%') is very small and low-contrast against the white background, making it difficult to read without magnification in a board presentation context.

findings.element: Oil Commentary — Supply Shock & Macro Transmission (top commentary block)
findings.detail: The commentary block contains a single very long run-on sentence that exceeds the 4-sentence maximum and uses hedging constructions ('does not fully capture', 'functioning as'). Style guide requires 2–4 crisp sentences with no hedging filler.

findings.element: Section 2 — 'So what' callout boxes beneath Exhibits 3 and 4
findings.detail: 'So what' commentary boxes appear below the charts in Sections 1 and 2 rather than preceding the first chart on the tab. Per style guide, fc-note commentary must precede the first chart it annotates.

findings.element: Section 2 — Full Oil Impact Chain (Exhibit 6) phase status badges
findings.detail: The 'PHASES ACTIVE' counter tile ('4 of 8 transmitting') appears visually disconnected from the phase node list below it, with inconsistent vertical alignment relative to the 'SHOCK' and 'ELAPSED' tiles beside it.

findings.element: Section 3 — Airlines & Freight sector impact table vs. other sections
findings.detail: Section 3 has noticeably more vertical whitespace above and below the table compared to the tighter spacing in Sections 1, 2, and 4, creating an inconsistent rhythm across the tab.
